description:
Answers two different questions about an IP address or domain, and keeps them apart: do we HOLD it, and what sits NEXT to it.

`held` is an exact yes or no, with `held_in` naming the lane that answered (iocs, the published blocklist lane, or the graph). `neighbors` is group membership in our indicator graph: the same /24 for an IPv4 address, the same registrable domain for a domain, with a real count (or "200+" with truncated:true when the scan hit its bound). `neighbor_summary` says what those neighbors are: how many are attributed to which actor or malware family, from how many lanes. A range we carry that covers the address, with no exact record, is reported as `block_coverage`, never as a detection.

`strength` is a single word for a hurried reader: none, adjacent-only, single-lane, multi-lane or corroborated. Read `caveats` before trusting it: a shared hosting platform or cloud range makes neighbors co-tenants, not related infrastructure, and the response says so when it applies.

Use it after `enrich-ioc`, or first, when the question is "is this part of something": a scanner next to a known C2, a lookalike domain on a campaign's registrar, a clean address in a dirty /24. Keyed Pro and Enterprise callers also get the neighbor rows themselves (`neighbors.sample`) to pivot on with `enrich-ioc`; free and anonymous callers get the counts and the summary.

Not consulted: our own edge observations (blocks, honeypot hits). Read-only. Hashes and URLs are not graph nodes; use `enrich-ioc` for those.

indicator.description: An IPv4 address or a domain.

limit.description: Max neighbor rows returned to Pro and Enterprise callers. Default 10. Counts and the summary do not depend on it.

name: correlate
title: Correlate an indicator: do we hold it, and what is next to it
